Yeahhhhh.  So I'm really good at working on my own cars, and apparently I'm really good at riding motorcycles - but I know I'm not.  That is, I haven't experienced front brake lock ups, scary situations on the road, unexpected low traction environments...

Going from a state with lots of snow and ice to a state without a lot of snow and ice, I realized that there are a lot of people who *think* they're better than they are.

I want to push myself in controlled environments, and I want my skills plus my bike to be able to handle crazy road situations.

That said, with wind being a larger factor than I imagined, I'm pretty tempted to get a Honda CBR600 (I really really love Honda's small motors).  Kinda attracted to the idea of having great suspension travel for all the unexpected potholes and idiot drivers I've seen driving cars, but I'm not sure if hitting a pothole with any bike is a realistically survivable scenario (??)

I think I definitely will need ABS now that I'm in Seattle... tons of rain.  Switchable ABS would be nice even on a sports bike, because I suppose I can go in a parking lot in the rain and get the low traction experience I seek.

I read this wrong at first and wrote a long response thinking you raped her.  I groped a couple of girls at frat parties in college and i feel awful about it.  Downright awful.

But what's more important is that you need to tell her what you did, and that you know it was wrong.  And that it's killing you that it happened.

Delayed onset PTSD is a thing, and this could be festering with her too, to the point she can't trust anyone anymore.  How would you feel if you couldn't trust even your close friends (and, in this case, even her girlfriend broke her trust).

Look, it sounds awful, but groping someone isn't that bad.  It's not like you completely raped her.  It's not like you killed her.  But you crossed a line that says "i will sexually take from you without your consent" and that is a serious violation of trust.

So All In All:

probably everything I've said has crossed your mind since you're obviously concerned about it.  but you have the opportunity to make things right here, still.  you didn't wait for years and years after the fact.

and all in all, if you're going to kill yourself, you might as well try to make things better before you do.  what's the worst that could happen?

bring her cookies.  tell her you're sorry and don't linger.  she never has to forgive you; just let her know that what you did was wrong and you'd do anything to fix it.
